buckets.title: Motion in a Plane (CBSE Class XI, Unit II Kinematics) with labelled JEE extensions
buckets.badge_reason: Learners must move between vector algebra and plane kinematics while keeping one frame, one clock and each model's validity conditions in view.

curriculum_mappings.locator: Class XI Theory, Unit II Kinematics, Chapter 3 Motion in a Plane

conventions.statement: Declare one x-y frame (origin and axis directions) before writing any component; every component of one problem uses that frame.
i-hat and j-hat are unit vectors along the declared x and y axes.

scope.covers: Scalars and vectors, equality, multiplication by a real number, graphical and analytical addition and subtraction, resolution into rectangular components, motion in a plane with constant acceleration, projectile motion and uniform circular motion, as listed by the CBSE 2026-27 curriculum and the NCERT chapter; five JEE extension microtopics are carried as labelled extensions.

capabilities.action: Classify a physical quantity as scalar or vector, draw a displacement from its end points alone, and judge whether two vectors are equal.
capabilities.success_criterion: Names direction as the deciding property, gives the same displacement for every path between fixed end points, separates path length from displacement magnitude, and calls two vectors equal only when magnitude and direction both match.

curriculum_mappings.locator: Class XI Unit II Chapter 3: scalar and vector quantities; position and displacement vectors; equality of vectors

capabilities.action: Predict the magnitude, direction and physical kind of a vector multiplied by a real number, including a negative number, zero, or a multiplier that carries its own dimension.
capabilities.success_criterion: Gives |lambda| times the original magnitude, keeps the direction for a positive multiplier and reverses it for a negative one, returns the null vector for zero, and names the new quantity from the product of dimensions.

curriculum_mappings.locator: Class XI Unit II Chapter 3: multiplication of vectors by a real number

capabilities.action: Add and subtract vectors by drawing them head to tail (or as a parallelogram from a common tail) and read the resultant's size and direction from the drawing.
capabilities.success_criterion: Places each tail at the previous head, draws the resultant from the first tail to the last head, forms A - B as A + (-B), and bounds the resultant between the difference and the sum of the magnitudes.

curriculum_mappings.locator: Class XI Unit II Chapter 3: addition and subtraction of vectors

capabilities.action: Resolve a plane vector into signed rectangular components from its magnitude and angle, and rebuild the magnitude and angle from the components.
capabilities.success_criterion: Writes A = A_x i + A_y j with A_x = A cos(theta) and A_y = A sin(theta), gives each component its correct sign from theta, and recovers A = sqrt(A_x^2 + A_y^2) with the angle placed in the right quadrant.

curriculum_mappings.locator: Class XI Unit II Chapter 3: unit vector; resolution of a vector in a plane, rectangular components

capabilities.action: Add or subtract any number of plane vectors by summing their components, and find the magnitude and direction of the resultant of two vectors from the law of cosines and the law of sines.
capabilities.success_criterion: Sums like components with their signs, rebuilds the resultant's magnitude and angle, and uses R^2 = A^2 + B^2 + 2AB cos(theta) only with theta taken between the vectors drawn tail to tail.

curriculum_mappings.locator: Class XI Unit II Chapter 3: addition and subtraction of vectors (analytical method using rectangular components)

capabilities.action: Find average and instantaneous velocity and average acceleration of a particle moving in a plane from its position vector, and read the velocity's direction as tangent to the path.
capabilities.success_criterion: Divides the displacement (not the path length) by the interval for average velocity, differentiates r(t) componentwise for v(t) and a(t), gives the magnitude and angle of v at a stated instant, and does not assume v and a are collinear.

curriculum_mappings.locator: Class XI Unit II Chapter 3: motion in a plane; position, velocity and acceleration vectors

capabilities.action: Solve plane motion with constant acceleration by writing the vector equations v = v0 + a t and r = r0 + v0 t + (1/2) a t^2 as two one-dimensional motions that share one time.
capabilities.success_criterion: Checks that the acceleration is constant before using the equations, finds the time from one axis, reuses it on the other axis, and recognises which general relations hold for arbitrary motion.

curriculum_mappings.locator: Class XI Unit II Chapter 3: motion in a plane, cases of uniform velocity and uniform acceleration

capabilities.action: Model a projectile, with air resistance neglected, as uniform horizontal motion plus vertical motion with constant acceleration g, and derive its path, time of flight, maximum height and range from that model.
capabilities.success_criterion: States the model's assumption, writes a_x = 0 and a_y = -g, finds event times from the vertical motion and reuses them horizontally, and uses the level-ground formulas only when launch and landing heights are equal.

curriculum_mappings.locator: Class XI Unit II Chapter 3: motion in a plane with uniform acceleration - projectile motion

capabilities.action: Find the angular speed, linear speed and centripetal acceleration of uniform circular motion and state the acceleration's direction.
capabilities.success_criterion: Uses omega = 2 pi / T (or 2 pi nu), v = omega R and a_c = v^2/R = omega^2 R, points a_c at the centre, and states that it has constant magnitude but is not a constant vector.

curriculum_mappings.locator: Class XI Unit II Chapter 3: uniform circular motion

capabilities.action: Find the velocity of one body relative to another, or relative to a moving frame, in two dimensions and use it for river-crossing, rain-and-umbrella and closest-approach situations.
capabilities.success_criterion: Measures both velocities in one common frame, forms v12 = v1 - v2 or v_PS = v_PS' + v_S'S as a vector triangle, and treats accelerations as frame-independent only between frames in uniform relative motion.

curriculum_mappings.locator: JEE (Advanced) 2026 syllabus, Physics, Mechanics: Relative velocity

capabilities.action: Solve a projectile launched from and landing on an inclined plane, or aimed at a point off the launch level, by resolving gravity along and perpendicular to the plane or by intersecting the trajectory with a line.
capabilities.success_criterion: Uses axes along and perpendicular to the incline with g_x = -g sin(alpha) and g_y = -g cos(alpha), takes the launch angle to the horizontal as alpha + beta, and does not use the level-ground time-of-flight formula.

curriculum_mappings.locator: Not named in the JEE (Advanced) 2026 syllabus; covered only by the general 'projectiles' entry

capabilities.action: Treat a bouncing projectile as two projectile flights joined by a collision, using the collision type to set the launch velocity of the second flight.
capabilities.success_criterion: Keeps the speed unchanged for an elastic rebound and finds the new direction before solving the next flight, states that kinetic energy is lost in an inelastic rebound while the momentum of the colliding system is conserved, and does not claim kinetic energy is constant during contact.

curriculum_mappings.locator: Not named in the JEE (Advanced) 2026 syllabus, which lists 'Elastic and inelastic collisions' and 'projectiles' separately

capabilities.action: Predict qualitatively how a drag force proportional to velocity changes a projectile's path, and use the terminal-velocity and work-energy ideas that such a force implies.
capabilities.success_criterion: States that linear drag opposes the velocity on both axes, so v_x decreases and the fall is steeper than the rise; says the 45 degree and parabola results no longer hold; and finds terminal conditions from a force balance.

curriculum_mappings.locator: Not in the JEE (Advanced) 2026 syllabus; only Stokes' law and terminal velocity are listed, under fluids

capabilities.action: Find the total acceleration of a particle moving on a circle with changing speed as the perpendicular sum of its centripetal and tangential accelerations.
capabilities.success_criterion: Computes a_c = v^2/r and a_T = d|v|/dt, combines them as perpendicular vectors, gives the angle to the tangent, and states that the net acceleration is central only when the speed is constant.
